item: Three comprehensions under a lock or a finally are functions of their own, so an interrupt cannot skip the release (R205)
summary: On CPython 3.13 a comprehension is inlined into its function and its filter-skip back-edge sits outside the exception table of the with/finally around it, so a KeyboardInterrupt delivered there skips the cleanup (measured on a minimal case: 12,283 of 12,491 interrupts). The tree-wide read-only scan (/mnt/project-files/audit-0.5.0/inputs/comprehensions-in-try-report.md) found 100 such comprehensions in 68 functions under a with/finally/except BaseException; this moves the three Tier A sites with a plausible chain to boot or a CLI into small functions of their own, body unchanged: upgrade_sources_to_composite_key (four comprehensions between the try and the BEGIN; the finally turns foreign-key enforcement back on; reached from init_db), DamageRegistry.confirmed_damage (two, under self._lock), lane_engine (one, under the module _lock). tests/test_r205_comprehensions_under_cleanup.py reads the compiled code with the dis helper of test_gates_survive_an_interrupt.py and is red with the old code (3 failed). Reachability in the report is by bare function name, depth 4, a hint and not a proof; Tier B (31 worker-only or unreached functions) and Tier C (30 session or file closes that process exit reclaims) are left as audit items, and versioned/store.py dispose_lane (same lock, no chain found) is the nearest sibling not converted.
